title: Brazilian-Style Fish and Prawn Stew with Coconut and Peppers
summary: Chunks of white fish and juicy prawns gently simmered in a vibrant coconut sauce with sweet peppers, tomato and chilli, finished with lime and coriander. Served from the pot with fluffy white rice.
equipment: wide casserole or deep frying pan (28-30 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: skinless firm white fish fillet (such as cod, hake or haddock), cut into 4 cm pieces
raw peeled and deveined king prawns
fine sea salt or table salt
dendê (red palm) oil, or olive oil plus 1 tsp sweet paprika
red chilli, seeded and finely chopped
ripe tomatoes, cut into thin wedges
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the seafood
steps.text: Toss the fish with half the lime juice, half the garlic and the salt and pepper, then toss the prawns separately with the rest of the lime and garlic. Cover and chill for 15-30 minutes, but no longer. Lime acid starts to firm and whiten the surface of the fish, so a short marinade seasons without turning it chalky.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then put it in the saucepan with the 450ml water and bring to the boil. Cover, cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it off the heat for 10 minutes. Rinsing removes loose starch, and the resting time lets the grains finish steaming into separate, fluffy rice.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Heat 1.5 tbsp of the palm oil in the wide casserole over medium heat and soften the onion for 4-5 minutes. Add the peppers and chilli for 5 minutes, then the tomatoes for 3-4 minutes, until they begin to collapse. Layering the vegetables this way gives each time to soften and sweeten.

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Pour in the coconut milk, add the salt and half the coriander, and simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, stirring now and then. You want it slightly thickened and coating the vegetables. A gentle simmer keeps the coconut milk smooth, while a hard boil can make it split.

steps.title: Add the seafood
steps.text: Nestle the fish into the sauce in a single layer and spoon some sauce over the top. Cover and simmer gently for 3 minutes, then tuck in the prawns, cover again and cook for another 3-5 minutes. The prawns should be pink, curled and opaque, and the fish should flake easily and read at least 63°C in the thickest piece; adding it late keeps it in big, moist chunks.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Drizzle with the remaining palm oil and scatter over the rest of the coriander. Bring the pot to the table and serve with the rice and lime wedges for squeezing.

tips: A common mistake is stirring once the fish is in, which breaks it into shreds; spoon the sauce over instead and shake the pan gently.
If you use olive oil instead of palm oil, stir the paprika into the oil at the start for colour.
Keep the marinating time within 30 minutes so the fish stays tender and silky.
Taste the sauce before adding the seafood and adjust the chilli heat then, as it is harder to fix later.
storage: Cool within 2 hours, refrigerate in a covered container and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently on the hob until piping hot (74°C), stirring carefully to keep the fish whole.
